title: Lock a pressure washer gun's trigger, then swap its red nozzle for the green one, holding the coupler's collar back
instruction: Swap the pressure washer's red 0-degree nozzle for the green 25-degree one, safely. First slide the gun's trigger lock to locked (it covers the red mark), before either hand comes near the nozzle. Then hold the coupler's spring collar pulled back with one hand while the other pulls the red nozzle out and lays it in the empty red slot of the nozzle holder, takes the green nozzle from its slot and pushes it into the coupler; then let go of the collar so it snaps forward and locks the nozzle in. Never bring a gripper near the nozzle while the trigger is unlocked. Then take both arms back to where they started.
context: A pressure washer's hose stays pressurized after the machine stops, and a red 0-degree jet can cut skin: the trigger lock goes on before a hand goes near the nozzle. A quick-connect coupler holds its nozzle until its spring collar is pulled back, and the collar snaps forward the moment it is let go, so one hand holds the collar back while the other takes the nozzle out or puts the next one in.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A black foam pad 17 x 33.4 cm and 2.5 cm thick, from 17 to 34 cm forward and from 0.4 cm right to 33 cm left of the centre line, fixed. (2) Lying on its side on the pad, a pressure washer's trigger gun (1.4 kg): a yellow ABS body 16 cm long, 4.6 cm wide and 4 cm thick from 14 to 30 cm left of the centre line, with a black rubber grip 9 cm long angled back toward the arms, a black trigger and trigger guard, and a steel hose swivel and a stub of black hose at the grip's end; and a black steel lance 1.3 cm thick running 13 cm to the right from the body, its axis 30 cm forward and 4.5 cm above the table, ending past the pad in a brass quick-connect coupler (2.1 cm across) with a knurled steel collar 2.7 cm across and 3.8 cm long. The collar slides 1.1 cm back along the coupler and a spring pushes it forward (about 2.2 N held back 1 cm); held back 6 mm or more it opens the coupler. (3) Plugged into the coupler, pointing right, a red 0-degree nozzle (25 g): a steel plug stem 0.9 cm across and 1.2 cm long, a red body 1.7 cm across and 3 cm long and a steel tip; its back face sits 5 cm right of the centre line. (4) On top of the gun's body above the trigger, the trigger lock: an orange slide 1 x 1.2 x 1.2 cm at 30.8 cm forward and 18.5 cm left, with a red mark beside it on the arms' side; it slides 1.8 cm toward the arms (it moves when pushed with more than about 1.5 N and stays where it is left), covering the red mark and uncovering a green one; slid 1 cm or more it is locked. (5) To the right, a black ABS nozzle holder, fixed: a base 20 x 7.5 x 0.8 cm with five slots 4 cm apart, from 20 to 36 cm forward. In each slot a nozzle lies left to right, its stem to the left on a notched rubber post and its tip on a narrow post, its back face 15.5 cm right of the centre line and its axis 3.5 cm above the table, with a coloured dot in front of the slot: red (empty), yellow (15 degrees), green (25 degrees, a loose nozzle like the red one), white (40 degrees) and black (soap). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. The trigger is locked while its slide is 1 cm or more toward the arms from where it starts. A nozzle comes out of the coupler only while the collar is held back (6 mm or more), and is free of it once its back face is 1.6 cm out of the seat. A nozzle whose stem goes into the open coupler (its axis within 4 mm and 15 degrees of the coupler's) is caught in it; pushed in to within 4 mm of seated, it is locked in when the collar is let go. The red nozzle is in its slot when it is out of the coupler and its back face's middle is within 1.5 cm sideways and 1.2 cm in height of where a nozzle lies in that slot, its axis within 20 degrees of the slot's. 0.0 once a gripper's TCP (the point between its fingertips) has come within 7 cm of the coupler's seat while the trigger was not locked. Otherwise, at the end: 0.0 with the trigger not locked; 1.0 with the trigger locked, the red nozzle in its slot, the green nozzle locked in the coupler and both arms back where they started (each gripper's TCP within 5 cm of its start); 0.75 with the trigger locked, the red nozzle in its slot and the green one locked in; 0.5 with the trigger locked and the red nozzle in its slot; 0.25 with the trigger locked. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the gun and both nozzles still.
reset_notes: Slide the trigger lock back to off, put the red nozzle back in the coupler and the green one in its slot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the trigger lock and the collar are slider joints (the lock held where it is left with up to 1.5 N); the coupler's balls are a rule: a joint keeps a nozzle on its axis, held at the seat while the collar is forward, free to slide while it is held back. No water or pressure is simulated; nozzles are about 1.3 times real size. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
